pr_title: feat: ignoreBrowserWarnings option to ignore browser console warnings
pr_body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->
<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->

Users will sometimes go into devtools when we're using module federation and may see some warnings about non-strict singleton versions. There's currently not a way to hide these in production. Then some of our customers thought there was something wrong who knows. With an extra option `ignoreBrowserWarnings` that operates basically like `ignoreWarnings` we can hide these warnings in production while also preserving them in other environments.

fixes https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/16374

<!-- In addition to that please answer these questions: -->

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

New webpack option similar to ignoreWarnings, but only operates on browser console warnings and is only an array of regex's

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes copied two existing tests and added the option in webpack

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

No

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

<!-- List all the information that needs to be added to the documentation after merge -->

Should go in docs right by here: https://webpack.js.org/configuration/other-options/#ignorewarnings
Also since these are really for module federation, there's probably a page there that would benefit from mentioning the option

<!-- When your changes are merged you will be asked to contribute this to the documentation -->

issue_context.title: Hide Invalid Non-Strict Singleton Versions on Production Console
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template or we'll close your issue -->

## Feature request

<!-- Issues that contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->
<!-- Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of webpack. -->
<!-- Check if this feature needs to be implemented in a plugin or loader instead -->
<!-- If yes: file the issue on the plugin/loader repo -->
<!-- Features related to the development server should be filed on this repo instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**

`index.js:2 Unsatisfied version x.y.z from ------- of shared singleton module ----- (required ^x.y.z)` warnings should not appear on production console.

**What is motivation or use case for adding/changing the behavior?**

End users on browsers see these errors and think there's something wrong with the page.

**How should this be implemented in your opinion?**

Provide a setting to hide these warnings and/or only show them during build: 

https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/0bc3a2ea02ba85e23e4d1e01b4b1f15fb27b5c1d/lib/sharing/ConsumeSharedPlugin.js#L308-L310

https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/0bc3a2ea02ba85e23e4d1e01b4b1f15fb27b5c1d/lib/sharing/ConsumeSharedRuntimeModule.js#L118-L124

**Are you willing to work on this yourself?**
yes

review_comments: To be hoesntly we still contain unused code in bundle, but we really don't need, just do more complex check and don't problem it when we have `ignoreBrowserWarnings: true`, although terser/swc remove them...

I just pushed an extreme version of this. I think we should probably just set these `var warn` to empty functions. This extreme version isn't particularly maintainable although the test coverage seems really good so maybe it's fine. It would basically be just to save a few lines of source in the browser that we had before anyways.

To be clear, I was saying I don't really like this version. It's harder to maintain and seems very error prone. Are there any downsides besides an extra line of code in the browser? I strongly think we should just have a `var warn` where it's an empty function when browser warnings are ignored and `console.warn` otherwise.

@alexander-akait are you good with the current state or is there some medium ground? I am concerned about conditionally removing every time a warn is called in these two runtime modules as it's very error-prone and some future editor could easily introduce an inadvertent error.
